# Gantt chart syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-gantt/grammar/gantt.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Gantt syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `gantt` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; `#name;` / `#123;` entities
read as opaque text that no rule takes apart; and a line break appended. Keywords are matched
without regard to case.

Statements need no separator: each starts with its own keyword, or is a task, whose text runs
to its first `:`; `title` and `section` take the rest of the line (a bare one takes the next
line), settings run to a `#`, `;` or the end of the line. A task's data is
`[tags,] [id,] [start,] end`; v12's DB reads it, the grammar does not take it apart.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A gantt chart is `gantt`, then statements.

```ebnf
diagram = Header document EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = gantt ;
```

```ebnf
document = { statement | NL } ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Setting
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr
          | Section
          | Task
          | Click ;
```

A setting: `dateFormat`, `axisFormat`, `tickInterval`, `includes`, `excludes`,
`todayMarker`, `inclusiveEndDates`, `topAxis`, `weekday <day>` or `weekend <day>`.

```ebnf
Setting @Setting = dateFormat
                 | inclusiveEndDates
                 | topAxis
                 | axisFormat
                 | tickInterval
                 | includes
                 | excludes
                 | todayMarker
                 | weekday_monday
                 | weekday_tuesday
                 | weekday_wednesday
                 | weekday_thursday
                 | weekday_friday
                 | weekday_saturday
                 | weekday_sunday
                 | weekend_friday
                 | weekend_saturday ;
```

`title <text>`: the chart title.

```ebnf
Title @Title = title ;
```

`accTitle: <text>`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = acc_title acc_title_value ;
```

`accDescr: <text>` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = acc_descr acc_descr_value
                   | acc_descr_multiline [ acc_descr_multiline_value ] acc_descr_multiline_end ;
```

`section <name>`: starts a section; the tasks after it are drawn in it.

```ebnf
Section @Section = section ;
```

`<text> :<data>`: a task, e.g. `Design :done, a1, 2024-01-01, 3d`.

```ebnf
Task @Task = task_text taskData ;
```

`click <ids> href "<url>"` and/or `call <function>(<args>)`, either first.

```ebnf
Click @Click = click_keyword click_id [ click_end ] ( callback [ link ] | link [ callback ] ) ;
```

```ebnf
callback = call_keyword callbackname ( callback_empty_args | callback_args_open callbackargs callback_args_close ) ;
```

```ebnf
link = href_keyword href href_end ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `open_directive`, `acc_title`, `acc_descr`, `acc_descr_multiline`, `click`, `href`, `callbackname`, `callbackargs`.

Every rule ignores case: a rule for `ab` also matches `AB` and `aB`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | open_directive | `%%\{` | push(open_directive) | `%%{` with no directive name after it: jison begins a start condition the grammar never declares, so the next character is a lexical error. |
| INITIAL | acc_title | `accTitle\s*:\s*` | push(acc_title) | `accTitle: …` and `accDescr: …` take the rest of the line; `accDescr { … }` runs to `}`. |
| acc_title | acc_title_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | acc_descr | `accDescr\s*:\s*` | push(acc_descr) |  |
| acc_descr | acc_descr_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | acc_descr_multiline | `accDescr\s*\{\s*` | push(acc_descr_multiline) |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | acc_descr_multiline_end | `\}` | pop |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | acc_descr_multiline_value | `[^}]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `%%[^\n]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[^}]%[^\n]*` |  | A `%` after any one character but `}` (a line break too) comments out the rest of the line: `5% buffer :3d` vanishes. |
| INITIAL | — | `%[^\n]*\n*` |  | A `%` where a token starts comments out the rest of the line and the line breaks after it. |
| INITIAL | NL | `\n+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `\s+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | href_keyword | `href\s+"` | push(href) | `href "<url>"`: the link a click opens, after `click <ids>`. |
| href | href_end | `"` | pop |  |
| href | href | `[^"]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | call_keyword | `call\s+` | push(callbackname) | `call <function>(<args>)`: the function a click calls, after `click <ids>`. |
| callbackname | callback_empty_args | `\(\s*\)` | pop |  |
| callbackname | callback_args_open | `\(` | pop push(callbackargs) |  |
| callbackname | callbackname | `[^(]*` |  |  |
| callbackargs | callback_args_close | `\)` | pop |  |
| callbackargs | callbackargs | `[^)]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | click_keyword | `click\s+` | push(click) | `click <ids> …`: what clicking the tasks with these ids does, `href` and/or `call`. |
| click | click_end | `[\s\n]` | pop |  |
| click | click_id | `[^\s\n]*` |  | The task ids after `click`, comma-separated, no blanks. |
| INITIAL | gantt | `gantt\b` |  | `gantt`: starts a gantt chart. |
| INITIAL | dateFormat | `dateFormat\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `dateFormat <format>`: how the task dates are written, e.g. `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| INITIAL | inclusiveEndDates | `inclusiveEndDates\b` |  | `inclusiveEndDates`: an end date includes its whole day. |
| INITIAL | topAxis | `topAxis\b` |  | `topAxis`: draws the date axis above the chart too. |
| INITIAL | axisFormat | `axisFormat\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `axisFormat <format>`: how the axis labels the dates, e.g. `%Y-%m-%d`. |
| INITIAL | tickInterval | `tickInterval\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `tickInterval <n><unit>`: the axis tick spacing, e.g. `1week`. |
| INITIAL | includes | `includes\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `includes <days>`: days drawn as work days though `excludes` names them. |
| INITIAL | excludes | `excludes\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `excludes <days>`: days a task skips, e.g. `weekends`, `friday`, `2024-01-01`. |
| INITIAL | todayMarker | `todayMarker\s[^\n;]+` |  | `todayMarker off` or `todayMarker <style>`: hides or styles the today line. |
| INITIAL | weekday_monday | `weekday\s+monday\b` |  | `weekday <day>`: the day week ticks start on. |
| INITIAL | weekday_tuesday | `weekday\s+tuesday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | weekday_wednesday | `weekday\s+wednesday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | weekday_thursday | `weekday\s+thursday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | weekday_friday | `weekday\s+friday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | weekday_saturday | `weekday\s+saturday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | weekday_sunday | `weekday\s+sunday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | weekend_friday | `weekend\s+friday\b` |  | `weekend friday\|saturday`: the first day of the weekend `excludes weekends` skips. |
| INITIAL | weekend_saturday | `weekend\s+saturday\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | date | `\d\d\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b` |  | A date where a statement starts: no statement starts with one. |
| INITIAL | title | `title\s[^\n]+` |  | `title <text>`: the chart title, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | accDescription | `accDescription\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `accDescription …`: lexed, but no statement takes it; write `accDescr: …`. |
| INITIAL | section | `section\s[^\n]+` |  | `section <name>`: the tasks after it belong to the section, up to the next one. |
| INITIAL | task_text | `[^:\n]+` |  | A task's text, up to its `:`. |
| INITIAL | taskData | `:[^#\n;]+` |  | A task's data after `:`, up to `#`, `;` or the end of the line. |
| INITIAL | colon | `:` |  | A `:` with no task data after it. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
